To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the assimilate export rate from leaves is controlled by the level of apoplast-derived metabolites and that this control represents a mechanism of assimilate sink strength.

(1) assimilates are transported through the plant apoplast and, after entering leaves, are reexported to the phloem; (2) assimilate demand in leaves is determined by changes in the apoplast content of metabolites; and (3) the mechanism of assimilates transport through the apoplast is controlled by the pH value of the cell wall solution.
assimilate transport is controlled by the apoplastic pool of metabolites.
